The body clause is a comparison of states ('differs from the code its body pin was taken from'), but the claim-pin clause names an event ('has been restated or removed since'). DEF-aligned-link compares digests at one revision. DEF-code-link and DEF-current-trial make the claim digest depend only on current content: the fingerprints of the node and its dependencies, and the set of those dependencies. So a restatement that is later undone leaves the digest equal to the pin. DEF-restatement says outright that a staged candidate's content can change ('whether its candidate's own content changes'), and nothing ties that change to a revision. So a change and its undoing can both fall between two revisions. I checked whether this scenario survives. It can be saved only by reading 'revision' as a pair of a commit and a ledger moment. Then r0, read in between the two restatements, would be 'the first revision', and the link did stop reading aligned there. But that makes alignment 'at a revision' change over time, and DEF-aligned-link and the claim's own 'exactly at the revisions at which it is aligned' do not allow that. A second scenario, below, does not depend on this reading at all. I also tried the body clause: once the body pin is taken to be the digest of the code it came from, DEF-code-link's injectivity ('differs whenever that code differs') makes it hold, and a code revert is covered by 'every later one at which it is not aligned'. That attack failed. Suggested restatement (the author's move): 'at which the statement or cited premises of its node or of a node it depends on, or the set of those nodes, differ from those its claim pin was taken from, or its node is outside the premise graph'.

counterexample: Needed premises: (1) fidelity: a link is reported as aligned exactly when it is aligned as DEF-aligned-link defines it. (2) scope: every file git tracks that declares a code link is scanned; or else the claim is restricted to scanned files, and the mention clause keeps 'in a comment or docstring of a scanned file'. (3) the claim-pin condition stated as a difference of state from the pinned version (node or dependency statement or cited premises, or the dependency set, differ from those the claim pin was taken from, or the node is outside the premise graph), not as 'has been restated or removed since'. Otherwise a premise is needed that a restatement between two revisions cannot be undone before the next one, which DEF-restatement contradicts. (4) DEF-premise-graph cited, so that a removed id names no node in the premise graph and the premise graph at a revision is defined. (5) a pin, when taken, equals the digest of the code or claim it was taken from.
reasoning: I checked each clause. (a) 'Reads aligned exactly at the revisions at which it is aligned': AXM-links-never-silent gives totality (every link is reported as aligned or as not aligned, with why), not fidelity. Nothing says the verdict matches DEF-aligned-link, so the derivation's step 'so it reads aligned exactly where it is aligned' does not follow. (b) 'The first revision at which ... restated or removed since': not entailed (see the counterexample trial). Restatement is an event, alignment compares states, and DEF-restatement lets a staged node change and change back with no revision between. The derivation's step 'a fingerprint differs whenever the statement or the cited premises differ, which DEF-restatement calls restating' treats 'has been restated since the pin' as if it meant 'differs from the pinned version'. Also, 'a removed node is in no premise graph' is asserted without a cited premise. DEF-premise-graph is mentioned inside DEF-restatement but not cited, and DEF-proof-state describes admission only at the head revision plus the ledger. That leaves 'the premise graph at' a non-head revision undefined, because staged proposals live in the ledger, not at a revision. (c) 'At that revision and every later one at which it is not aligned, it is reported with why': entailed for links in scanned files once (a) is added. 'Later' assumes revisions are linearly ordered, which git history is not, but the clause holds at every revision anyway, so this does no harm. (d) Mention clause: the claim drops AXM's scope 'in a comment or docstring of a scanned file'. Nothing requires a dangling id in a string literal, in non-comment code, or in an unscanned file to be reported, so the clause as written is broader than its source. (e) No-proof-state clause: entailed. AXM-links-never-silent states it directly, and it also follows from DEF-report (no record appended, no declaration changed), DEF-code-link (a link is neither a trial nor a ledger record) and DEF-proof-state (computed only from the admitted version and the trials recorded). (f) Body clause: entailed, given that a pin equals the digest of what it was taken from. 'Taken from' implies this, but DEF-code-link only calls it 'a body pin on the region'.

The negation of the restatement conjunct can be derived from the same premises. DEF-restatement allows a staged candidate's content to change and be restored between two revisions. DEF-current-trial makes a fingerprint depend only on statement and cited premises. DEF-code-link makes the claim digest depend only on those fingerprints and the dependency set. DEF-aligned-link then makes the link aligned at the first revision after the restatements. So 'its node has been restated since its claim pin was taken and it is aligned at the first such revision' is consistent with, and in fact derived from, the premises. For the first sentence (report fidelity) and the scope of the link and mention clauses, the premises decide neither the claim nor its negation: AXM-links-never-silent fits a correct reporter, a reporter that always says aligned, and a scanner that covers only some tracked files or only comments. Only the no-proof-state clause is decided in the claim's favour (AXM-links-never-silent says it directly). Because the premises do not settle the claim as a whole, the outcome is not sound.

Built scenarios to satisfy every premise while breaking one clause of the claim. None worked. (1) Body case: the pin was taken from code c0, and at revision r the region holds c1, which differs from c0 once comments and layout are set aside. DEF-code-link fixes the body digest as a function of the code alone, so it cannot vary by revision, and that function separates any two different codes. So digest(c1) != digest(c0) = pin, and DEF-aligned-link fails. Variants: the header was copy-pasted from another region, so the pin was taken from that region's code; the pin was taken from working-tree code that changed before the commit; the region's markers moved so the region grew. Each one either makes the case false or makes the digest differ from the pin. A pin that was never taken (typed by hand) makes the case's premise false, so the claim asserts nothing about it. (2) Node outside the declared graph: the node exists only as a staged proposal, which DEF-code-link excludes from the declared graph. Or it is declared but cites a premise that is not admitted, so no build admits it. Or a dependency's restatement cites a missing node, which takes the node out of the graph through the citation chain. Each fails DEF-aligned-link's membership conjunct directly. (3) Claim side: a dependency D whose statement changed, where D was or was not a dependency when the pin was taken. If it was, the id-keyed fingerprint differs. If it was not, the dependency set differs. Either way the claim digest differs from the pin. Further variants: two dependencies swap statements, which changes D1's fingerprint by id, so the premise's 'differs whenever any of those differs' applies. Premises reordered: the claim and the fingerprint use the same term 'premises it cites', so the clause and the digest move together. A change and revert before r makes the case false at r. A change two edges up the chain counts, because 'depends on' is defined by paths. A dependency set that shrinks or grows hits the set clause. (4) Revision quantifier: tried revisions earlier than, or on another branch from, the one where the pin was taken. The case is evaluated against the link as declared at r and the state its pins came from, and the axiom is stated per revision, so no revision escapes. (5) Mention clause: tried an id named only by a staged proposal, an id in a file under the ledger directories, and an id in a file declaring tdlp:foreign-ids. The claim and the axiom agree on every one. (6) Proof state: tried a reader that writes the header lines it suggests. Under DEF-report, output that appends to the ledger or changes a declaration is not a report, and the axiom states directly that producing these reports changes no proof state.

Checked each clause against the premises. 'Reads aligned exactly when it is aligned' restates AXM-links-never-silent's first clause. The listed cases are now one-directional: each case implies 'not aligned'. The claim does not say the list is complete, which is what made the first wording fail. Body case: the pin equals the digest of the code it was taken from (DEF-code-link). The digest separates different codes (DEF-code-link), so it differs from the pin, and DEF-aligned-link's body-pin conjunct fails. Membership case: DEF-aligned-link's membership conjunct, directly. Claim case: fingerprints differ whenever a statement or the cited premises differ (DEF-current-trial). The claim digest differs when any fingerprint differs or the dependency set differs (DEF-code-link). So the claim digest differs from the claim pin. 'Depends on' uses DEF-premise-graph's paths, so the transitive dependencies are covered. 'At every revision at which the case holds': DEF-aligned-link is evaluated at r, and the axiom reports with why at every revision, so this follows with nothing added. The mention clause has the same scope as the axiom: comment or docstring, scanned file, not foreign, names no node in the declared graph and no code region. Its only wording difference is that it drops 'at that revision'. DEF-code-link defines the declared graph only at a revision, and the only revision in the sentence is the scanned file's, so that is the only binding available. No-proof-state clause: the axiom states it directly. It also follows a second way: a report appends no record and changes no declaration (DEF-report), and the proof state depends only on the declarations, the staged proposals and the recorded trials (DEF-proof-state). 'A link' in the second sentence is not a gap: 'aligned' is defined only for code links (DEF-aligned-link), and motivated-by is not one (DEF-code-link), so 'a link is not aligned' can only refer to code links. No clause needs a fact about what the code does: digest injectivity, pin taking and the reporting are all premises.

Tried to derive NOT(claim) from the same premises: some revision where a link reads aligned but is not aligned (or the reverse), a listed case where the link is aligned or goes unreported, an unreported mention, or a report that changes a proof state. Each one contradicts the axiom, either directly or through DEF-aligned-link combined with the digest properties above. So NOT(claim) can be derived only if the premises are inconsistent. They are not, as one model shows: let the body digest be the normalized code itself, the fingerprint be the pair (statement, cited premises), the claim digest be the id-keyed map of fingerprints over the node and its dependency set, and the reader report what the axiom requires and write nothing. Every premise holds in that model, and so does the claim. The premises therefore decide the claim, and in its favour.

subject: BRN-links-stale-when-either-side-moves
text: Wording points that could not be turned into trials and carry no proof weight. (1) The mention sentence drops the axiom's 'at that revision'. It is bound to the scanned file's revision only because DEF-code-link defines the declared graph per revision; writing it out would remove a reading that binds it to HEAD. (2) The second sentence says 'A link' where the first says 'a code link'. It is resolved only because 'aligned' is defined only for code links and motivated-by is excluded; 'A code link' would say so directly. (3) The claim-side case 'depends on a different set of nodes' leaves 'than when its claim pin was taken' implicit. (4) The body and claim cases rest on DEF-code-link's idealisation that the digests separate any two different inputs. A fixed-length hash satisfies this only up to collision, so whether it holds is an implementation-fidelity question for component-belief (CTR-code-links-aligned), not for this branch.

reasoning: I tried five attacks aimed at the new code-link clause. (1) Showing something from another revision: a code region beside node N carries a header line that pins N's statement or fingerprint from an earlier revision, and the page displays it. Every premise holds, and the claim still stands. The header text belongs to a scanned file 'of that commit', so it is shown as committed at the named revision. It is code-region text, not a declaration. DEF-snapshot also says independently that it 'takes every declaration it shows from that commit and from no other version of it'. (2) A broken tag or mention names an id that exists only in uncommitted edits or in a later revision. The snapshot shows the mention and its broken status, never that declaration: uncommitted declaration files are named as carrying edits and are not shown. So the first sentence holds. (3) Changing a proof state through a link: a code region linked to a lemma might add support or a citation. DEF-snapshot says 'a code region is never a node or an edge of the premise graph it shows'. DEF-premise-graph admits edges only from citations. DEF-proof-state's proven condition has no code-link term (cited premises, axiom or definition roots, current-trial coverage, consensus, no falsified trial). So the graph, the admitted versions and the proof states are unchanged. (4) Showing a second proof state: the link's state, as DEF-aligned-link gives it, could display something proof-like beside a node that differs from the node's state in the build. DEF-snapshot says it shows the proof state DEF-proof-state gives in that build 'and no other', and it evaluates the link state 'at that commit'. A link state is therefore not a second proof state for the node. (5) Side effects: the snapshot writes its page into a directory that a later code-link scan reads, or the scan itself writes something. The snapshot writes only two files, in a directory with no declaration file and no part of the ledger. It makes no commit, so the commit's scanned files cannot change. It appends no record of any provenance, so no trial, amendment or artifact appears, and by AXM-no-belief-write-path no measured belief moves. Under AXM-commit-is-approval, uncommitted working-tree files feed no proof state. None of the five scenarios keeps every premise true while breaking a clause of the claim.

I checked each clause against the cited premises. 'Every declaration shown is as committed at the one revision it names' is stated directly in DEF-snapshot: it resolves head to one commit before reading, names only that commit, and takes every declaration from it. The new clause does not weaken this, because it puts code regions in 'the scanned files of that commit', evaluates link states 'at that commit', and says a region is never a node or an edge. 'Every proposal shown is the one staged in the ledger as read' is stated directly in DEF-snapshot. The proof-state clause is DEF-snapshot's 'for each lemma and branch in that build ... the proof state DEF-proof-state gives that node in that build, and no other'. 'Changes no measured belief' follows from: no record appended + DEF-belief-eligible (belief-eligible evidence is a ledger trial record) + DEF-ledger + AXM-no-belief-write-path. The axiom's qualifier 'under the declarations in effect' is covered because the snapshot changes no declaration, makes no commit and does not move head. 'Changes no proof state' follows from these facts: the snapshot does not move head, stages, restates or withdraws no proposal, and appends no trial or amendment, so the DEF-premise-graph build and every fingerprint are unchanged and DEF-current-trial gives the same current set. Its two written files are uncommitted and outside the declarations and the ledger, so AXM-commit-is-approval excludes them, and the never-a-node-or-edge clause shuts out code links. DEF-aligned-link is not cited. The claim needs nothing from it, because the claim says nothing about which link state is shown, only that the link is not a declaration, not a proposal, not a proof state and not a graph element, and DEF-snapshot settles each of those on its own. I found no assumption that would need the code to judge.

To derive NOT(claim), the cited premises would have to yield one of three things. (a) A shown declaration from a revision other than the named commit: DEF-snapshot rules this out explicitly, and the new clause binds code regions and link states to the same commit. (b) A shown proof state that differs from the build's: ruled out by 'and no other', and a code region is never a node or an edge, so links cannot change the build. (c) A snapshot that moves a belief or a proof state: ruled out because no record of any provenance is appended, no declaration changes, no commit is made, head stays put, and the only files written are uncommitted and outside the declarations and the ledger. The one possible source of tension is DEF-aligned-link. If it gave a link state from some other revision, DEF-snapshot's 'at that commit' would contradict it. But DEF-aligned-link is not among the premises, and from the cited premises its state is evaluated at the snapshot's commit, so no contradiction can be built from what is cited. The premises decide the claim, in its favour.

subject: DEF-snapshot
text: This note came out of verifying BRN-snapshot-shows-one-revision; it does not affect that branch, and I could not turn it into a trial. The restated DEF-snapshot now shows each code link's state 'as DEF-aligned-link gives it at that commit', yet it still says it 'shows no state for a contract and reads no evidence record'. Whether those two clauses can both hold depends on what DEF-aligned-link reads. If a link's alignment depends on a contract's state or on evidence records, DEF-snapshot contradicts itself. If it depends only on the commit's code, header pins and declaration fingerprints, there is no contradiction. DEF-aligned-link is not a premise of this branch, so I could not judge it from here. It is worth checking when DEF-aligned-link or a branch citing both definitions is verified.

counterexample: At head revision r, axiom A and branch B are declared. B cites A and L. L is not declared at r and has a staged proposal with statement S1 citing A. B's derivation rule names CTR-x. Premise graph (DEF-premise-graph): A, L and B are admitted, and B depends on A and L. Declared graph at r (DEF-code-link: declarations committed at r, no staged proposal): A is admitted; B is left out because L is absent, so B depends on no node there. B's claim digest at r is therefore determined by B's own fingerprint (its declaration's statement and premises) and the empty set. CTR-x's acceptance rule and tests are read against B's claim, and a pin p equal to that digest is written after CTR-x. Then L is re-proposed with statement S2 != S1, which restates L under DEF-restatement, and a revision r' is committed that changes no declaration. At r', B's declaration and fingerprint are unchanged, the declared graph is unchanged, and B still depends on nothing in it, so B's claim digest at r' equals p. By DEF-cited-measurement CTR-x is reviewed, and by AXM-cited-measurements-reviewed it reads reviewed at r'. Yet L, a node B depends on, has a statement other than when the pin was taken, and the claim says CTR-x is then not reviewed and is reported with why. Second instance: L is withdrawn instead. B leaves the premise graph, so it depends on a different set of nodes, yet its digest and its reviewed status are unchanged. A staged-only branch B' citing declared A gives a third instance under the same literal reading: B' is absent from the declared graph, so restating A at a new revision leaves B''s digest equal to its pin.
reasoning: Attacks tried that FAILED: (1) a digest collision between two claim states: DEF-code-link stipulates the digest differs whenever a fingerprint or the dependency set differs, so it cannot happen. (2) A single edit that writes a pin and also edits the statement: the node is restated, but by the statement change. DEF-cited-measurement says a pin edit as such changes neither statement nor premises, so the pin clause stands. (3) An amendment: DEF-current-trial's validity condition turns only on amendments appended to the trial itself, and no premise makes writing a derivation-rule pin append one. A pin written to a staged branch is a re-proposal with the same statement and premises, which DEF-restatement's governing clause does not count as restating. (4) Uncited-contract and no-proof-state clauses: both are in AXM-cited-measurements-reviewed nearly verbatim. Attack that SUCCEEDED: the listed cases use 'depends on' and 'statement', which DEF-premise-graph and DEF-restatement define over the premise graph, staged proposals included. The claim digest of DEF-code-link is computed over the declared graph, committed declarations only. A branch with a staged-only ancestor separates the two, as in the scenario below. Every premise holds there and the listed-case clause fails.

counterexample: Unstated assumption: that 'a node its branch depends on', 'statement or cited premises' and 'a different set of nodes' in the listed cases mean the same things in the declared graph at that revision (committed declarations, no staged proposal). The claim needs one of two fixes. Fix 1: restate the cases over the declared graph, e.g. 'a node its branch depends on in the declared graph at that revision has a declared statement or cited premises other than when its pin was taken, or the set of nodes it depends on there differs'. Fix 2: add a premise that a branch not admitted to the declared graph at a revision has no claim digest there, so none of its cited measurements is reviewed at that revision.
reasoning: The derivation rule switches meaning mid-argument. It quotes DEF-code-link's digest 'of every node it depends on in the declared graph'. It then concludes 'in each listed case the digest differs', but the listed cases are stated with unqualified 'depends on' (a path in the premise graph, per DEF-premise-graph) and with candidate statements (staged proposals included, per DEF-restatement). The two relations agree only when the branch is declared and none of its ancestors is staged-only. Checked and entailed: the first sentence is AXM-cited-measurements-reviewed ('reported as reviewed exactly when it is reviewed'). The no-pin case follows directly from DEF-cited-measurement. On the pin clause: DEF-cited-measurement makes a pin edit change neither statement nor premises, so it is no restatement under DEF-restatement. Admission depends on cited premises alone, so every build is unchanged and the target stays in the graph. Fingerprints depend only on statement and premises, so recorded fingerprints still match id for id. Writing a pin is not an amendment to any trial, so validity is untouched. A combined statement-plus-pin edit restates the node through its statement, not through its pin. The uncited-contract clause matches the axiom only if the opening 'At every revision' also covers it: the claim drops 'declared at that revision', but the branch-side wording 'no branch's derivation rule names' is identical. The no-proof-state clause is AXM's last sentence verbatim, and it also follows from DEF-report (no record appended, no declaration changed) with DEF-proof-state (computed from graph place, admitted version and recorded trials alone). On terminology: 'cited measurement' is never a citation in DEF-premise-graph's sense, because contract ids are not nodes and a derivation rule is not the premises a node cites, so no edge is created. No step here confuses the two senses.

Take the configuration the premises allow: a declared branch with a staged-only ancestor that is restated or withdrawn after the pin is taken. Under the literal reading of DEF-code-link, a non-admitted node's digest comes from its own fingerprint and its empty dependency set in the declared graph. From DEF-cited-measurement and DEF-code-link the premises then derive that the measurement IS reviewed, which is the negation of the listed-case clause. Under the competing reading, a node outside the declared graph has no claim digest, and the same premises derive NOT reviewed, which agrees with the claim. Both readings fit the premises as written, so the premises do not decide the clause. For the other clauses I could not derive a negation: the reviewed-iff-reviewed sentence, the no-pin case, the case where every ancestor is declared, the pin edit restating nothing and keeping trials current, the uncited-contract report, and no proof-state change.

subject: BRN-cited-measurements-reviewed-while-the-claim-stands
text:
Observations from verification that I could not turn into trials (no proof weight):
(1) The word "cited" now has two senses. In DEF-premise-graph, "Only a citation is an edge" refers to premises. A "cited measurement" is a contract id named in a derivation rule and adds no edge. Nothing in this claim mixes them up, but "cited premises" and "cited measurement" sit side by side in one sentence. Two possible fixes: DEF-premise-graph could say that naming a contract in a derivation rule is not a citation in its sense, or the new nodes could say "named measurement".
(2) DEF-cited-measurement identifies a cited measurement by its contract id, but "its branch" assumes a single branch. Two cases are left undefined: one contract id named by two branches, only one of which pins it, and one id named twice in a single rule, once pinned and once not. Reading it as a (branch, contract id) occurrence would settle both.
(3) In the uncited-contract sentence the claim drops "declared at that revision". It matches the axiom only if the opening "At every revision" also covers that sentence.
(4) DEF-restatement's "its candidate becomes another record with different content" could be read to make re-proposing a staged branch only to write a pin a restatement. The governing clause, "statement or the premises it cites change", says otherwise. Spelling that out would remove the ambiguity.
(5) This branch's own evidence, CTR-trial-ledger-replay, carries no pin. By its own claim it would read not reviewed.

reasoning: Attacks tried, every premise held fixed. (1) The staged-only scenario that refuted the first wording: B is declared at R and cites X, which is undeclared but has a staged proposal. B is in the premise graph but not in the declared graph, so it has no claim digest. Case 'branch not in the declared graph' covers it: not reviewed, and DEF-cited-measurement agrees. The reverse direction also fails. If B is in the declared graph at R, every node it transitively cites is declared and admitted, and a declared id's only candidate is its declaration (DEF-premise-graph). So B's dependency set and every dependency's statement are the same in the declared graph and in the premise graph, and staged proposals can no longer make a case fire that the digest ignores. (2) B itself only staged: by DEF-cited-measurement no cited measurement exists, so the claim says nothing about it. A contract named only by B is uncited in both the claim and AXM-cited-measurements-reviewed, whose scopes are word for word the same ('branch declared at that revision'). (3) Do the cases fail DEF-cited-measurement? A pin equals B's claim digest as it stood when taken, and a branch outside the declared graph has none, so any pin is a declared-graph digest at the revision it was taken. Take a node N that B depends on now with a statement different from when the pin was taken. If N was in the pin-time set, its fingerprint differs, so the digest differs. If it was not, the set differs, so the digest differs. A node that has left the set is the 'different set' case. B's own statement change changes B's fingerprint. So every enumerated case gives digest != pin, which is not reviewed. (4) Revert: restate B at R1 and restore it at R2. The digest at R2 equals the pin again and the measurement is reviewed. That is consistent, because the claim scopes the cases 'at every revision at which that holds'. (5) A contract named twice in one rule is one pair, and the first pin counts. Named by two branches, it is two pairs, each with its own pin and digest. Neither yields a case-holds-yet-reviewed scenario. (6) A pin edit in the same commit as a statement edit: the commit restates B and its trials stop being current, but only because of the statement edit. Restatement and currency are functions of statements and cited premises alone, and the pin part contributes nothing. (7) Amendments: a pin is text in a derivation rule, which is a declaration change, and DEF-report separates that from a ledger append. So writing a pin appends no amendment, and trial validity is untouched. (8) A pin copied by hand from another branch, or taken while B had no digest: either way the pin is not 'taken by recording the branch's claim digest', which violates DEF-cited-measurement, so it refutes nothing. No scenario survived.

Clause by clause. 'Reads reviewed exactly when reviewed' and 'reported with why at every revision' come straight from AXM-cited-measurements-reviewed. 'No pin' and 'not in the declared graph' come straight from DEF-cited-measurement's reviewed condition, plus its sentence that a branch outside the declared graph has no claim digest. For the statement, cited-premises and dependency-set cases: DEF-code-link's digest at a revision covers the fingerprints of B and of its declared-graph dependencies, and differs when any of them differs or the set differs. DEF-current-trial makes a fingerprint differ when a statement or the cited premises differ. DEF-cited-measurement makes the pin equal the digest at the time it was taken. Together these give digest != pin. Statements are read in the declared graph at that revision, where each node's candidate is its declaration at that revision (DEF-code-link plus DEF-premise-graph), so 'has a statement' is not the head-time candidate. 'Restates no node': DEF-cited-measurement says a pin changes neither statement nor cited premises, and DEF-restatement's condition is exactly that those change. 'Every current trial current': the build depends on cited premises alone, fingerprints are unchanged, and no amendment is appended because a pin write is a declaration change, not a ledger record (DEF-report keeps the two apart). The uncited-contract clause restates AXM verbatim, with the same scope. 'No proof state changes' follows from AXM, and from DEF-report together with DEF-proof-state. I found no clause that needs knowledge of the implementation. The one idealization, that every pin is a correctly taken declared-graph digest, is stated in DEF-cited-measurement itself.

To derive NOT(claim) I would need one of four things. (a) An enumerated case that holds at a revision while the digest equals the pin. That is excluded, because DEF-code-link's 'differs whenever' covers changes to both fingerprints and the set, and the pin is the digest from when it was taken. (b) A measurement that reads reviewed while it is not reviewed. AXM excludes that. (c) A pin write that changes a statement or cited premises. DEF-cited-measurement excludes that. (d) A report that appends a record or changes a proof state. AXM, DEF-report and DEF-proof-state exclude that. The premises also decide the boundary cases instead of leaving them open: a branch outside the declared graph has no digest, the first pin counts, the uncited scope is branches declared at that revision, and the claim keeps silent on staged-only branches. So the premises are strong enough to decide the claim, and they decide it positively.

subject: BRN-cited-measurements-reviewed-while-the-claim-stands
text: Wording observations with no proof weight, found while verifying TRL-0319..0321. (1) 'Writing or changing a pin restates no node and leaves every current trial current' reads as the effect of the pin edit alone. If a commit also edits a statement, the commit restates. 'Writing or changing only a pin' would close off that reading. (2) DEF-cited-measurement does not say what a 'mention of that id' is when one id is a prefix of another (for example CTR-x and CTR-x-y). If a pin written after CTR-x-y were taken as CTR-x's pin, the 'first pin' rule would pick the wrong one. This matters for fidelity, not for the step, which holds under any fixed notion of mention. (3) The step relies on DEF-cited-measurement's idealization that every pin is a correctly taken declared-graph digest. A pin copied by hand from another branch, or written while the branch had no digest, is outside the premises. Whether such a string is reported as 'no pin' or as 'stale' is for the implementer.
